title: LedgerMath data API, version 1: one Series
description: v1/series/<id>.json: one Series, its summary and its newest Runs. A Series is the Runs of one benchmark, parameter set (params), build, instance type and Availability Zone ID. Under derivations, keyed <method name>_v<version>, is each Method's Derivation of it, at the same paths and in the same words as the Method's file of Derivations, with the Method's own definitions beside it, less what grows with every Run: the percentiles, the groups its split facts make and their facts and figures, how often each dump section changed, how many Runs it counts and does not, and the points of the newest Runs (newest_points; as many as newest_runs says). Every Run's point, and what differed between consecutive Runs, is in the file of the month the Run started in, which months lists with its address: the Series' points are those of its month files, oldest month first. The lists of Run ids behind each percentile and in each group are not repeated; each is recovered from those points by the rule its field's description gives. Each point also gives the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence: the Run file (evidence) and its boot's summary (boot_summary). Numbers are exactly as the Derivation holds them; a duration is in nanoseconds of the Run's clock unless its field's name says otherwise. The file changes when the Series gains a Run, a Method's words change, or a newest point's boot summary arrives. Version 1 only ever gains fields: a field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know, which is why no object in this schema forbids members it does not list. A new Method, or a new version of one, is a new key beside the old ones. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1.

schema.description: What this file is, and which version of its shape.

index.description: The address of the table of contents, v1/index.json.

id.description: The Series' id: the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of its key (benchmark, params, build, instance type, zone ID) as canonical JSON.

params.description: The parameter set, as each Run was given it (LM_PARAM_*).

build.description: The named build of the benchmark (static, dynamic).

instance_type.description: The EC2 instance type, as the provider names it.

availability_zone_id.description: The Availability Zone ID, as the provider names it.

runs.description: Runs in the Series, counted or not.

newest_run_started_at.description: When its newest Run started: the moment a citation of the Series as it stands names.

newest_runs.description: How many of the Series' newest Runs each Method's newest_points holds: this many, or every Run when the Series has fewer. The same in every Series file.

months.description: Every month in which a Run of the Series started (UTC, by the Run's start), oldest first, each with the address of its file. A month's file holds every point of its Runs, and changes only when a Run of that month is added or a point's boot summary arrives: once a month has passed, its file stays the same.

derivations.description: Each Method's Derivation of the Series, keyed <method name>_v<version>. Method series v1 derives every Series; Method requests v1 only those whose samples are requests, and its key is absent from the others.

time.description: UTC, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it.

definitions.description: How each number is made, in the Method's words, by name.

section.description: The dump section it is read from, if it is.

facts.description: A group's split facts and their values: a blob's sha256:<hex>, a section's canonical-json-sha256:<hex>, the sample count, the image ID.

url.description: The address of the month's file, v1/series/<id>/<yyyy-mm>.json.

runs.description: Runs of the Series that started that month, counted or not.

oldest_run_started_at.description: When the oldest of them started.

newest_run_started_at.description: When the newest of them started.

point_path.description: The Run file's path in the Runs repository, runs/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<id>.json, which is also its key under the evidence's address.

point_sha256.description: The sha256 of the Run file's bytes, in hex: what the Derivation cites.

point_boot_summary.description: The address of the summary of the boot the Run was part of, which accounts for every execution the boot was to run; null when the Runs repository held no summary of that boot when the file was made.

point_group.description: The group its split facts put it in.

point_counted.description: Whether the Method counts the Run. A Run it does not count is shown, with why, and is in no figure.

point_failure.description: Why it is not counted, or null.

series_v1.description: Method series, version 1: one number per Run, and the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles across Runs, for the Series and for each group. Its points are in the month files, under the same key.

split_on.description: The facts a Series is split into groups on, in order.

left_out.description: What is left out of a dump section before it is compared for the split, and why.

not_split_on.description: Facts the Runs record that do not split a Series, and why.

failed_runs.description: Runs it does not count: shown in their month's file with why, in no percentile.

percentiles.description: Across every counted Run of the Series, whatever its group.

sections.description: How often each dump section's hash changed in this Series.

newest_points.description: The points of the Series' newest Runs (newest_runs of them, or all when there are fewer), in time order: the same points, value for value, as their month's file holds.

series_point.description: One Run on the Series' chart, with the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence.

samples.description: Its counted samples, in stream order; empty when it is not counted.

sample.description: The sample's number in the stream.

ns.description: sample_ended.t minus sample_started.t, in nanoseconds of the Run's clock.

time_per_repetition_ns.description: The median of its samples' ns_per_repetition: the Run's one number, 0 or more. Null when it is not counted; and null when it is infinite, past a double's range, which JSON cannot hold: when it is the mean of its two middle samples' ns_per_repetition and their sum overflows (both near the top of a double's range; no real clock comes near). Such a Run is still counted, and still among the Runs of its Series' and group's time_per_repetition_ns percentiles.

bytes_per_repetition.description: As the benchmark observed it, a positive number. Null when it is not counted, or when the benchmark observed no bytes per repetition.

bytes_per_second.description: bytes_per_repetition × 10^9 / time_per_repetition_ns. Null when either is null; and null when the quotient is infinite, past a double's range, which JSON cannot hold: chiefly a counted Run that observed bytes per repetition and whose time per repetition is 0 (its median sample ended at the clock read it started at). Such a Run is still counted, and still among the Runs of its Series' and group's bytes_per_second percentiles.

stat.description: Percentiles of time per repetition across counted Runs. The Runs behind it are not listed: they are the counted points of the Series (of the group, for a group's), in time order, as the month files hold them. Every counted Run has a time per repetition. A counted Run's time per repetition is infinite, past a double's range, when it is the mean of its two middle samples' ns_per_repetition and their sum overflows (both near the top of a double's range; no real clock comes near): JSON cannot hold it, so its point shows null, and it is counted here all the same; a percentile taken from it, or interpolated towards it, is null.

p5.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite time per repetition.

p50.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite time per repetition.

p95.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite time per repetition.

bytes_per_second_stat.description: Percentiles of bytes per second across the counted Runs that observed bytes per repetition. The Runs behind it are not listed: they are the counted points of the Series (of the group, for a group's) whose bytes_per_repetition is not null, in time order, as the month files hold them. A Run among them whose bytes per second is infinite, past a double's range (chiefly one whose time per repetition is 0), cannot have it written in JSON: its point shows null, it is counted here all the same, and a percentile taken from it, or interpolated towards it, is null.

count.description: Counted Runs that observed bytes per repetition, a Run with an infinite bytes per second included.

p5.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite bytes per second.

p50.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite bytes per second.

p95.description: Null when it is infinite or undefined: taken from, or interpolated towards, an infinite bytes per second.

series_percentiles.description: time_per_repetition_ns is null when no Run counts; bytes_per_second is null when no counted Run observed bytes per repetition.

series_group.description: The Runs whose split facts are all equal. Lettered A, B, C… in the order each first appears; groups may interleave in time. Its Runs are not listed: they are the points whose group is its id, in time order, as the month files hold them.

runs.description: Runs whose before-dump or after-dump holds the section.

changed_within_run.description: Of those, the Runs whose before-dump and after-dump hold different hashes for it, or only one of which holds it.

pairs.description: Pairs of consecutive Runs in the Series at least one of whose before-dumps holds the section. A pair neither of whose before-dumps holds it is not counted for it, so the count can differ from section to section.

changed_between_runs.description: Of those, the pairs whose before-dumps hold different hashes for it, or only one of which holds it.

split_on.description: The split fact read from it, or null.

requests_v1.description: Method requests, version 1: each phase of a request, across the requests, within each Run and pooled across Runs, for the Series and for each group. Its points are in the month files, under the same key.

phases.description: The phases of a request, each an interval between two of its events, in nanoseconds of the Run's clock.

percentiles.description: The percentiles reported, and the fewest requests that support each.

precision.description: A pooled percentile is within this fraction of the exact percentile of the same requests.

request_facts.description: The facts each request records of its connection or of itself.

split_on.description: Method series v1's split facts, which give the same groups.

counted_runs.description: Runs this Method counts (exit 0, or 4 with failed requests).

failed_runs.description: Runs it does not count: shown in their month's file with why, in no figure.

pool.description: Every succeeded request of the Series' counted Runs, whatever their group.

items.description: Method series v1's group of the same letter: the same Runs. Its Runs are not listed: they are the points whose group is its id, in time order, as the month files hold them.

newest_points.description: The points of the Series' newest Runs (newest_runs of them, or all when there are fewer), in time order: the same points, value for value, as their month's file holds.

recorded.description: What the Series' Runs record beside their requests, counted or not: words for a reader, no figure.

regions.description: The box's Region as each Run's provider names it, with how many Runs.

services.description: The Service each Run names, with its inputs that are not secret, as delivered, and how many Runs.

request_stats.description: One phase over a set of requests, in nanoseconds: the count of requests, the least and greatest time, and each percentile the count supports (null when it does not), with how many requests are ranked at or above each one reported.

at_or_above.description: For each percentile reported, how many requests are ranked at or above it (ties counted by rank).

phase_stats.description: Each phase's statistics, by phase; a phase no request had is absent (dns, connect and tls over a kept connection).

pooled_phase.description: One phase pooled: its statistics, read from the summed histogram, and the histogram itself.

histogram.description: [bin, count] in bin order, no empty bin; the requests' histogram definition says which times each bin holds.

failure_count.description: Failed requests of one kind: where (phase) and what kind of failure, and how many.

phase.description: request_failed.phase; response for a complete response whose status is not 2xx; record for a request one of whose lines the binary withheld.

pool_summary.description: The pooled figures as they stood through one Run: the counted Runs that started at or before it. What a citation of an earlier moment is checked against.

pool.description: Every succeeded request of a set of counted Runs, pooled.

setups_failed.description: Setups of a kept connection that failed outside any sample.

by.description: The pooled figures again for the requests that had each value of a request fact, for each fact that took more than one value among the pool's requests.

runs.description: Counted Runs with at least one succeeded request of this value.

facts.description: Every value each request fact took among the pool's succeeded requests, a single value included, with how many requests had it.

requests_point.description: One Run of the Series, with the sha256 of its Run file and the addresses of its evidence.

exit_code.description: The binary's exit code, or null when a signal ended it.

counted_requests.description: Counted samples in its stream (counted requests); null when there was none to count.

succeeded.description: Of the counted requests, those that succeeded; 0 for a Run not counted.

failed.description: Of the counted requests, those that failed; 0 for a Run not counted.

phases.description: Its own succeeded requests' statistics per phase, exactly; empty for a Run not counted or one whose every request failed.

warmup_failure.description: How the warmup request failed, or null.

through.description: The Series' pooled figures through this Run; null before its first counted Run.

group_through.description: Its group's pooled figures through this Run, once the Series has had a Run of a second group by this Run; otherwise null. As it stood through this Run, as through is, so that a later Run does not change it: requests v1's Derivation also gives it, for every point of a Series that has more than one group, on the points before the Series' first Run of a second group, where every Run is of the first group and its figures are the Series' own; the API leaves those null, and they are that point's through.
